title_en: Taizhou Environmental Protection Federation v. Taixing Jinhui Chemical Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over compensation for environmental pollution tort

full_text_en:
Taizhou Environmental Protection Federation v. Taixing Jinhui Chemical Co., Ltd., et al. — Dispute over Environmental Pollution Tort Compensation

【Ruling Summary】

In environmental pollution cases, enterprises engaged in the production of hazardous chemicals and chemical products must exercise a high duty of care with respect to their main products and by-products. They must have a comprehensive understanding of whether their main products and the by-products generated during the production process are highly dangerous and whether they may cause environmental pollution. They must ensure that the production, sale, transportation, storage, and disposal of their main products comply with relevant legal provisions, and likewise ensure that the production, sale, transportation, storage, and disposal of their by-products comply with relevant legal provisions, so as to avoid causing damage to the ecological environment or creating a significant risk of such damage. Although rivers have a certain capacity for self-purification, the environmental capacity is limited. The large-scale dumping of by-product acids into rivers will inevitably cause severe damage to the water quality, aquatic flora and fauna, riverbeds, riverbanks, and the ecological environment downstream. If not remediated in a timely manner, the accumulation of pollution will inevitably exceed the environmental carrying capacity, ultimately resulting in irreversible environmental damage. Therefore, the fact that the water quality in certain sections has recovered cannot exempt the polluter from the obligation to carry out environmental remediation.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2015) Min Shen Zi No. 1366

Reapplying Applicant (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Taixing Jinhui Chemical Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 10, Xingang Road, Taixing Economic Development Zone, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Xu Jiangbo, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Bing, Attorney at Beijing Shidai Jiuhe Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Taizhou Environmental Protection Federation. Domicile: No. 18, Yonghui Road, Taizhou City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Tong Ning, Secretary-General of the Federation.

Agent ad litem: Chen Xiaojun, Attorney at Jiangsu Jianghao Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Wencan, Attorney at Jiangsu Tianzi Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance: Jiangsu Changlong Agrochemical Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 8, Tuanjiehe Road, Taixing Economic Development Zone, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Wang Weihua, General Manager of the Company.

Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance: Jiangsu Shimeikang Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 10-2, Xingang South Road, Taixing Economic Development Zone, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Wang Junhua, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Yabin, Attorney at Jiangsu Hengqiao Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance: Taixing Shenlong Chemical Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 3, Shugang Road, Taixing Economic Development Zone, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Jiang Desheng, Deputy General Manager of the Company.

Defendant at First Instance: Taixing Fu'an Chemical Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 8, Zhonggang Road, Taixing Economic Development Zone, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Qin Taohan, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Yu Xinsheng, Attorney at Jiangsu Youfang Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Taixing Zhenqing Chemical Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 10, Shugang Road, Taixing Economic Development Zone, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Yang Jiqun, Manager of the Company.

Reapplying Applicant Taixing Jinhui Chemical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinhui Company), in a case of dispute over compensation for environmental pollution tort with the Respondent Taizhou Environmental Protection Federation, as well as Defendants at First Instance and Appellants at Second Instance Jiangsu Changlong Agrochemical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Changlong Company), Jiangsu Shimeikang Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shimeikang Company), Taixing Shenlong Chemical Co., Ltd., and Defendants at First Instance Taixing Fu'an Chemical Co., Ltd. and Taixing Zhenqing Chemical Co., Ltd., being dissatisfied with the Civil Judgment (2014) Su Huan Gong Min Zhong Zi No. 00001 of the Jiangsu High People's Court, applied to this Court for retrial. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to review this case, and the review has now been concluded.

Jinhui Company applied for retrial on the following grounds:

(A) The amount of by-product acid dumped by Jiangzhong Company on behalf of Jinhui Company as determined in the second-instance judgment was erroneous. 1. According to the confessions of Dai Weiguo and others to the public security authorities, the amount of by-product acid dumped by Taizhou Jiangzhong Chemical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jiangzhong Company) on behalf of Jinhui Company was 653.08 tons. 2. The transportation expense invoices issued by Xinghua Xieyu Transportation Co., Ltd., Taixing Branch (hereinafter referred to as Xieyu Taixing Branch) showed that the amount of by-product acid transported for Jinhui Company was 1,702.27 tons. Since the second-instance court determined that the freight payments made by Jinhui Company were subsidies for dumping fees, the dumping amount should also be determined based on the figures on the transportation expense invoices issued by Xieyu Taixing Branch. 3. If calculated based on the sales invoices, Dai Weiguo and others began dumping the by-product acid sold by Jinhui Company to Jiangzhong Company in August 2012. Before that, the invoices issued by Jinhui Company to Jiangzhong Company for by-product acid amounted to 3,822.2 tons; the invoice for 455.42 tons of by-product acid issued by Jinhui Company to Jiangzhong Company on December 29, 2011, was recorded in the accounts in 2012 and was not dumped in 2012. These two amounts of by-product acid should be deducted from the total amount sold by Jinhui Company to Jiangzhong Company. Therefore, the amount of by-product acid dumped by Jiangzhong Company on behalf of Jinhui Company should be determined from figures such as 653.08 tons, 1,702.27 tons, etc.

(B) The determination in the second-instance judgment that Jinhui Company should pay environmental remediation costs was not based on facts. 1. The rivers involved in this case do not require remediation or compensation. Before the pollution, the water quality of Rutai Canal and Guma River was Class III. After self-purification, the water quality in 2013 remained Class III. The Taizhou Environmental Protection Federation did not submit evidence proving that the pollution caused any personal injury or property damage to others. Therefore, Jinhui Company should not bear environmental remediation costs or compensation for losses. 2. The second-instance judgment lacked confirmation and assessment of the ecological environmental damage to the rivers involved. Replacing ecological environmental damage with costs of water pollution remediation has no factual or legal basis. 3. The determination and calculation method of remediation costs were erroneous. The "Recommended Methods for Calculating the Amount of Environmental Pollution Damage" (hereinafter referred to as the "Recommended Methods") (Version I) issued by the Environmental Planning Institute of the Ministry of Environmental Protection established three methods: actual remediation cost method, virtual treatment cost method, and remediation cost method. The treatment cost method in the "Environmental Pollution Damage Assessment Technical Report on the December 19 Waste Acid Dumping Incident in the Guma River and Rutai Canal of Taixing City, Taizhou City" (hereinafter referred to as the "Assessment Technical Report") was based on Section 4.5.2 of the "Recommended Methods" (Version I), which determined the unit treatment cost for water body remediation using the chemical oxidation method, with a calculated unit treatment cost of RMB 700 per ton. Therefore, the treatment cost method in the "Assessment Technical Report" was actually the remediation cost method in the "Recommended Methods," with a sensitivity coefficient of 1.4 to 1.6 times. The calculated environmental remediation costs should be approximately RMB 50 million, of which Jinhui Company should bear RMB 8,757,855. Furthermore, in its complaint at first instance, the Taizhou Environmental Protection Federation claimed compensation from the six defendant companies for losses from water pollution, not environmental remediation costs. The second-instance judgment ordering the six defendant companies to bear environmental remediation costs exceeded the plaintiff's claims.

(C) The second-instance judgment applied the law incorrectly. 1. The "Recommended Methods" (Version I) was already invalid at the time of the second-instance proceedings, and the second-instance court did not conduct a new damage assessment appraisal based on the "Recommended Methods" (Version II). The "Recommended Methods" (Version II) provides for two methods: environmental remediation and ecological restoration, both premised on damage to the natural environment. However, in this case, there was no damage to the natural environment, and remediation should not be carried out. 2. Jinhui Company fulfilled its duty of care in selling the by-product acid. The contracts entered into between Jinhui Company and the buyers, stipulating the allocation of freight costs, fall within the regulatory scope of the Contract Law of the PRC and cannot be governed by the provisions of the Tort Liability Law.

(D) The Taizhou Environmental Protection Federation does not have the standing to initiate this environmental civil public interest lawsuit. The second-instance judgment's determination that it had standing as a plaintiff was erroneous.

(E) Jinhui Company is not the appropriate subject of liability in this case. Jinhui Company itself did not engage in any pollution acts such as discharge, dumping, or leakage, nor did it instruct others to do so. The disposal of the by-product acid by Jiangzhong Company after purchase is unrelated to Jinhui Company. There was no meeting of minds between the parties. Therefore, Jinhui Company should not bear tort liability for environmental pollution.

(F) The second-instance judgment cited Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law), which concerns affirming the original judgment, but actually rendered a modified judgment. This constitutes an error in the application of law.

(G) The content of Paragraph 4 of the main text of the second-instance judgment falls within the scope of enterprise autonomy. By placing the enforcement decision of this content in the hands of the competent administrative department for environmental protection and establishing an approval procedure, the second-instance judgment infringed upon Jinhui Company's autonomy as an enterprise.

(H) The Taizhou Environmental Protection Federation did not file lawsuits against other chemical enterprises that may have polluted the environment. The environmental civil public interest lawsuit filed by Friends of Nature Environmental Research Institute (Beijing Chaoyang District) against other local polluting enterprises, which was accepted by the court in accordance with the law, could affect the amount of liability borne by Jinhui Company. Jinhui Company applied for retrial based on Items 2, 6, and 11 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law.

Taizhou Environmental Protection Federation submitted its opinion stating:

(A) As an "organization concerned" as provided in Article 55 of the Civil Procedure Law, the Taizhou Environmental Protection Federation has the standing to initiate this environmental civil public interest lawsuit.

(B) Jinhui Company's so-called "sale" of by-product acid was in fact an illegal disposal act, and there is a causal relationship between it and the environmental pollution. 1. Jinhui Company's so-called "sale" was essentially an abandonment act, which does not meet the basic characteristics of a sales contract. Employees of Jinhui Company also admitted this when questioned by public security authorities. 2. Jinhui Company knew or should have known that Jiangzhong Company did not have the qualifications and capability to dispose of the by-product acid. In their records dated April 24, 2013, Dai Weiguo and Yao Xueyuan respectively stated that Jinhui Company knew that they definitely did not have the qualifications and capability to dispose of the by-product acid. 3. There is a causal relationship between Jinhui Company's act of handing over the by-product acid to Jiangzhong Company for disposal and the environmental pollution. Although Jinhui Company did not itself engage in acts of discharge, dumping, or leakage that polluted the environment, Jinhui Company knew or should have known that Jiangzhong Company and other entities did not have the qualifications and capability to treat the by-product acid; Jinhui Company knew that the payments it made were insufficient to cover the costs of proper, harmless disposal of the by-product acid; and by handing over the by-product acid, which had no value to Jinhui Company, to Dai Weiguo and others of Jiangzhong Company for processing, it not only provided the dumpers with a source of pollution but also objectively enabled the dumpers to obtain illegal profits.

(C) The amount of by-product acid dumped by Jiangzhong Company on behalf of Jinhui Company as determined in the second-instance judgment was correct. 1. The data cited by Jinhui Company in its retrial application were all based on the amounts recorded in Dai Weiping's ledger. However, Dai Weiping's ledger was incomplete in terms of both recording time and content. 2. Jinhui Company's quotation of the criminal defendants' confessions was taken out of context. (1) Dai Weiguo and Yao Xueyuan had already confirmed in the interrogation record dated August 8, 2013, that they had dumped 19,361.16 tons of by-product acid from Changlong Company and Jinhui Company. (2) Jinhui Company selectively extracted partial confessions of criminal defendants, incorrectly claiming that the dumping of the by-product acid involved began in August 2012. The actual dump time should be the end of 2011. 3. Yang Jun, Vice General Manager of Jinhui Company, clearly stated in the inquiry record dated October 10, 2013, that Dai Weiguo, Yao Xueyuan, and others balanced the accounts by providing Jinhui Company with transportation expense invoices or oil invoices. Therefore, Jinhui Company's calculation of the amount of by-product acid dumped by Jiangzhong Company based solely on transportation expense invoices was one-sided.

(D) The environmental remediation costs determined in the second-instance judgment were legal and reasonable. 1. The polluted rivers involved in this case require remediation. The dumping of large quantities of by-product acid into the rivers caused severe damage to the water body, aquatic life, riverbed, and other water ecological environments. The severity of the harm necessitates remediation. The environmental announcements issued by the local government concerning water quality testing only tested routine water quality indicators and did not fully cover the overall condition of the water quality. The test results of the water quality in the areas where the dumping occurred do not reflect the extent of damage to the rivers caused by the pollution. 2. The calculation method for the environmental remediation costs determined in the second-instance judgment was correct. The experimental value method used in the "Assessment Technical Report" was calculated merely from the perspective of "consuming Changjiang River water to reduce acidic pollution." It only calculated the cost of reducing the destructive potential of the pollution source itself and was not an assessment of environmental remediation costs. It was precisely because the actual environmental remediation costs were difficult to calculate that the virtual treatment cost method was applied, which is consistent with the "Recommended Methods." 3. Regarding which version of the "Recommended Methods" should be used. At the time the harmful acts occurred, only the "Recommended Methods" (Version I) existed; the "Recommended Methods" (Version II) was issued after the first-instance trial concluded. During the second-instance proceedings, Jinhui Company never claimed that the basis of the "Assessment Technical Report" had become invalid or applied for a new appraisal. Moreover, in the "Recommended Methods" (Version II), the virtual treatment cost method remains a commonly used method for environmental value assessment.

(E) The second-instance judgment's citation of Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law as the procedural basis for the judgment was correct. 1. The basis of the second-instance judgment was the finding that the first-instance judgment "had clear findings of fact and correct application of law." Among the items in Article 170, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law, only Item 1 specifies the circumstance where the facts are clearly found and the law is correctly applied. 2. The second-instance judgment affirmed the first-instance judgment regarding the entities responsible for environmental remediation, the items requiring compensation, and the amount of environmental remediation costs. It merely set certain conditions for the payment and setoff of the environmental remediation costs. These provisions did not change the findings of fact or application of law in the first-instance judgment. Instead, they were judicial explorations and innovations made by the second-instance court with the aim of preventing and controlling environmental pollution at the source, reflecting the second-instance court's environmental protection philosophy of combining judicial prevention with judicial punishment. 3. On the one hand, Jinhui Company argued that the conditions set for setoff in the second-instance judgment had no legal basis. On the other hand, Jinhui Company expressed approval of the provision that 40% of the environmental remediation costs could be offset by technology upgrade expenses, and it had already applied to the relevant competent authorities for such a setoff during the execution of the judgment in accordance with the second-instance judgment.

(F) Jinhui Company's claim that the setoff conditions in the second-instance judgment restricted its enterprise autonomy is a misunderstanding. The purpose of establishing certain procedures for the setoff of environmental remediation costs in the second-instance judgment was to guide enterprises in focusing on technological transformation, turning waste into treasure, promoting recycling, and reducing and avoiding environmental damage from by-product acid.

(G) The existence of other polluters or the omission of other polluters in this case does not affect the fairness of the judgment. This case did not calculate environmental remediation costs based on the overall environmental pollution damage result, but rather calculated them based on the type and quantity of pollutants dumped by each polluter. The judgment did not exempt or reduce the environmental tort liability of any other potentially existing polluters, nor did it increase the environmental tort liability of the six defendant companies, including Jinhui Company. Jinhui Company's retrial application lacks factual and legal basis, and it requests that the application be dismissed.

In the pre-trial conference convened by this Court, Jinhui Company confirmed that it was applying for retrial based on Items 1, 2, 6, and 11 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law. At the same time, Jinhui Company submitted three new pieces of evidence to this Court: 1. The Criminal Judgment (2014) Tai Zhong Huan Xing Zhong Zi No. 00001 of the Taizhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province, intended to prove that the amount of by-product acid dumped by Jiangzhong Company on behalf of Jinhui Company as determined in the second-instance judgment was erroneous. 2. The Civil Ruling (2015) Tai Zhong Huan Gong Min Su Chu Zi No. 00001 of the Taizhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province, intended to prove that there were other polluting enterprises, such as Jiangsu Zhongdan Chemical Technology Co., Ltd., involved in the environmental pollution liability case. 3. The Civil Ruling (2015) Su Huan Gong Min Su Zhong Zi No. 00001 of the Jiangsu High People's Court, intended to prove that the amount of environmental remediation costs that Jinhui Company was ordered to bear in the second-instance judgment was erroneous.

Taizhou Environmental Protection Federation expressed its opinion on the above evidentiary materials, stating: 1. The Criminal Judgment (2014) Tai Zhong Huan Xing Zhong Zi No. 00001 of the Taizhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province submitted by Jinhui Company cannot prove that the determination of the amount of by-product acid dumped by Jiangzhong Company on behalf of Jinhui Company in the second-instance judgment was erroneous. The determination in that judgment regarding the amount of by-product acid dumped by Jiangzhong Company on behalf of Jinhui Company is consistent with the second-instance judgment in this case. 2. The Civil Ruling (2015) Tai Zhong Huan Gong Min Su Chu Zi No. 00001 of the Taizhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province and the Civil Ruling (2015) Su Huan Gong Min Su Zhong Zi No. 00001 of the Jiangsu High People's Court submitted by Jinhui Company cannot prove that the amount of environmental remediation costs that Jinhui Company was ordered to bear in the second-instance judgment was erroneous. The above two rulings were only rulings on the procedural aspects of the case, not judgments on the merits, and cannot determine whether there were other tortfeasors for the water body involved in this case during the same period. Even if other tortfeasors existed, it would not affect the amount determined in this judgment. Therefore, the three new evidentiary materials submitted by Jinhui Company are not new evidence in the retrial review stage of this case.

This Court finds that this case is a civil retrial review case. According to Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law and Article 395 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this Court should review whether the grounds for retrial asserted by the reapplying applicant are established. Among the seven disputed issues in this case, the review of the first, second, fifth, and seventh disputed issues is to determine whether Jinhui Company's retrial application meets the criteria of Item 6 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law; the review of the third, fourth, and fifth disputed issues is to determine whether Jinhui Company's retrial application meets the criteria of Item 2 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law. In addition, regarding the new evidentiary materials submitted by Jinhui Company under Items 1 and 11 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law and the issue of whether the second-instance judgment exceeded the parties' claims, this Court will evaluate them in conjunction with the relevant disputed issues.

(1) Whether the determination in the second-instance judgment that the Taizhou Environmental Protection Federation had standing as a plaintiff in this case has a legal basis.

Article 55 of the Civil Procedure Law stipulates: "For conduct that pollutes the environment, infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of numerous consumers, or otherwise damages the public interest, the organs and relevant organizations prescribed by law may file a lawsuit with the People's Court." The Taizhou Environmental Protection Federation was a social organization registered and established with the Taizhou Civil Affairs Bureau on February 25, 2014. Its purpose is to focus on the sustainable development strategy, implement the Scientific Outlook on Development, play a bridging and linking role between the government and society around achieving Taizhou's environmental protection goals and safeguarding the public's environmental rights and interests, and promote the progress and development of environmental protection in Taizhou and all of humanity. Its business scope includes providing environmental policy recommendations, safeguarding the public's environmental rights and interests, conducting environmental publicity and education, and providing policy and technology consulting services. The Taizhou Environmental Protection Federation filed this environmental civil public interest lawsuit on August 4, 2014, pursuant to Article 55 of the Civil Procedure Law, which has sufficient legal basis. The Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, which officially came into effect on January 1, 2015, does not apply to this case. Jinhui Company's assertion that the Taizhou Environmental Protection Federation does not have standing as a plaintiff in this case lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

(2) Whether the second-instance judgment's determination that there is a causal relationship between Jinhui Company's act of disposing of the by-product acid it produced through sale and the environmental pollution damage to the Gumagan River and Rutai Canal is sufficiently grounded

Jinhui Company and Jiangzhong Company entered into an "Industrial and Mineral Products Purchase and Sale Contract," stipulating that Jinhui Company would sell by-product acid to Jiangzhong Company at a monthly quantity of 800 tons, with prices fluctuating with the market. According to the interrogation records of Yao Xueyuan and Dai Weiguo at the public security organ, as well as the inquiry records of Jinhui Company's Deputy General Manager Yang Jun and Safety Production Director Dai Jiandong at the public security organ, it is known that under the sluggish trading market for by-product acid, in order to dispose of the by-product acid as quickly as possible, Jinhui Company actually sold the by-product acid at a price of RMB 1 per ton, while simultaneously subsidizing Jiangzhong Company RMB 20 per ton for transportation costs, and settling accounts based on the actual quantity of by-product acid shipped out by Jiangzhong Company. The seller delivering goods and the buyer paying the corresponding price constitutes the essential nature of a sales contract. Jinhui Company, as the seller, sold by-product acid, while the buyer, Jiangzhong Company, only paid RMB 1 per ton; instead, Jinhui Company paid RMB 20 per ton in transportation costs or other subsidies to Jiangzhong Company. This kind of subsidized sale is clearly inconsistent with the basic characteristics of a sales contract.

By-product acid is a hazardous chemical, subject to specific regulations for its production, sale, transportation, storage, and disposal. Article 29, Paragraph 1 of the Water Pollution Prevention and Control Law of the People's Republic of China prohibits the discharge of oil, acid liquids, alkali liquids, or highly toxic waste liquids into water bodies. By-product acid, as a by-product generated during the production of chemical products by an enterprise, if it cannot enter the market, should be disposed of by an institution qualified to handle hazardous waste in accordance with national laws and regulations. As a producer of hazardous chemicals and chemical products, an enterprise needs to fully understand whether its main products and the by-products generated during the production process of its main products are highly hazardous and whether they may cause environmental pollution; it needs to ensure that the production, sale, transportation, storage, and disposal of its main products comply with relevant laws and regulations, and also needs to ensure that the production, sale, transportation, storage, and disposal of its by-products comply with relevant laws and regulations, so as to avoid causing damage to the ecological environment or creating a significant risk of such damage. The by-product acid generated during Jinhui Company's production and operation is a hazardous chemical, subject to specific regulations for its production, sale, transportation, storage, and disposal. Jinhui Company should have a high duty of care regarding the disposal of by-product acid. From the interrogation records of Dai Weiguo, Yao Xueyuan, and others who carried out the dumping, and the inquiry records of Yang Jun and Dai Jiandong at the public security organ, it is evident that Jinhui Company knew that Dai Weiguo, Yao Xueyuan, and others were dumping by-product acid into the river but did not stop them. Although Jinhui Company did not directly carry out the dumping, it knew that the by-product acid market was sluggish and that harmless treatment would require high costs. By using methods such as subsidizing transportation costs, it handed over the by-product acid to Jiangzhong Company, which lacked the qualifications for disposal, and long-term allowed Jiangzhong Company to dump the by-product acid into the river, causing large-scale pollution of the Rutai Canal and Gumagan River waters, seriously harming the public interest and the public's environmental rights. There is a causal relationship between its conduct and the damage resulting from the water pollution of the Rutai Canal and Gumagan River, and it shall bear tort liability.

(3) Whether the second-instance judgment's order that Jinhui Company bear the responsibility for ecological environment restoration is sufficiently grounded

Although rivers have a certain self-purification capacity, environmental capacity is limited. The large-scale dumping of by-product acid into water bodies will inevitably cause severe damage to the river's water quality, aquatic flora and fauna, riverbed, riverbanks, and the ecological environment downstream. If restoration is not carried out in a timely manner, the accumulation of pollution will inevitably exceed the environmental carrying capacity, eventually causing irreversible environmental damage. Therefore, the fact that water quality in certain parts of the water body has recovered cannot be used as a reason to exempt the polluter from the environmental restoration responsibility it should bear.

The Taizhou Environmental Protection Federation applied for Professor Lv Xiwu from the School of Energy and Environment at Southeast University to appear as an expert assistant at the first-instance trial to provide opinions on the appraisal opinion and the professional issues involved in this case. Professor Lv Xiwu opined that the act of dumping hazardous waste into water bodies directly caused damage to the regional ecological environment functions and natural resources. The costs required either for restoring the damage caused to the ecological environment resources of the Yangtze River inland waters or for artificial intervention measures to reduce the risks caused by the pollution to an acceptable level would far exceed the costs of directly treating the pollutants. Due to the flow of river water and self-purification, even if the water quality at the dumping site has recovered, this cannot deny the damage once caused to the aquatic ecological environment. Appraisal expert Professor He Qihuan from Nanjing University of Science and Technology, when questioned in court, also stated that it is impossible to calculate the actual cost of artificial intervention, or it is difficult to calculate such costs, and the virtual disposal cost method can be used to calculate the losses.

The water environment is fluid, pollution acts occur instantaneously, and the site of damage cannot be restored. This situation falls under the circumstance where environmental restoration costs are difficult to calculate as stipulated in the Recommended Methods (Version I), and the virtual disposal cost method may be used to calculate environmental restoration costs. Moreover, there is no essential difference between the provisions on the virtual disposal cost method in the Recommended Methods (Version II) and those in (Version I). The second-instance judgment calculated the environmental restoration costs by taking the treatment cost of the by-product acid from Jinhui Company that was dumped by Jiangzhong Company, as determined in the Assessment Technical Report, multiplied by the quantity dumped, and then multiplied by the lower limit of 4.5 times the recommended multiple of 4.5-6 for the functional sensitivity of Class III surface water environments. This calculation was not improper.

Upon examining the first-instance complaint of the Taizhou Environmental Protection Federation, although the claim was expressed as compensation for losses from water environment pollution, the facts and reasons section clearly indicated that this compensation amount was for environmental restoration costs. The second-instance judgment ordering Jinhui Company to bear the environmental restoration costs did not exceed the claims of the parties.

(4) Whether the second-instance judgment's determination that the quantity of by-product acid from Jinhui Company dumped by Jiangzhong Company was 5,460.18 tons has a factual basis

After Changlong Company and Jinhui Company delivered the by-product acid to Jiangzhong Company, Jiangzhong Company did not record the specific quantities of by-product acid from Changlong and Jinhui that were dumped, but directly dumped the received by-product acid into the river. However, both Changlong Company and Jinhui Company recorded the sales quantities of by-product acid by issuing VAT invoices. The interrogation records of Dai Weiguo and Yao Xueyuan at the public security organ recorded the total quantity of by-product acid from both Changlong Company and Jinhui Company that was dumped by Jiangzhong Company. Therefore, to ascertain the quantity of by-product acid from Jinhui Company dumped by Jiangzhong Company, it is necessary to ascertain the quantities of by-product acid sold by Changlong Company and Jinhui Company to Jiangzhong Company and the quantity of by-product acid dumped by Jiangzhong Company. The second-instance judgment, based on the VAT special invoices for the sale of by-product acid by Changlong Company and Jinhui Company, as well as the confessions of Dai Weiguo, Yao Xueyuan, Ding Jinguang, and others at the public security organ, determined that the quantities of by-product acid sold by Changlong Company and Jinhui Company to Jiangzhong Company were 17,598.92 tons and 8,224.97 tons, respectively. The total sales volume of the two companies, minus 7,170.71 tons sold by Jiangzhong Company with invoices, and minus 1,508.92 tons sold by Jiangzhong Company without invoices, leaves 17,143.86 tons dumped by Jiangzhong Company. Allocating according to the proportion of the respective sales quantities of Changlong Company and Jinhui Company, the quantity of dumped by-product acid attributable to Changlong Company was 11,683.68 tons, and that attributable to Jinhui Company was 5,460.18 tons. Since the by-product acids from Changlong Company and Jinhui Company were mixed and dumped by Jiangzhong Company, it was impossible to accurately ascertain the quantities dumped from each company. The second-instance judgment, by determining the respective quantities of dumped by-product acid according to the proportion of the two companies' sales, applied a reasonable method of determination.

Jinhui Company's claim, based on some interrogation records of Dai Weiguo and Yao Xueyuan at the public security organ and some transportation expense receipts, that the second-instance judgment erred in determining the quantity of its by-product acid dumped by Jiangzhong Company, cannot be sustained.

When applying for retrial to this Court, Jinhui Company submitted the Criminal Judgment No. (2014) Tai Zhong Huan Xing Zhong Zi No. 00001 of the Taizhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province as new evidence, purportedly to prove that the second-instance judgment erred in determining the quantity of its by-product acid dumped by Jiangzhong Company. Upon review, the content of the aforementioned criminal second-instance judgment is the determination of the crimes of the suspects in this case who dumped the by-product acid. The criminal second-instance judgment states that Dai Weiguo and Yao Xueyuan, jointly or in collusion with Jiang Qiaohong, collected 5,460.18 tons of by-product acid from Jinhui Company under the name of Jiangzhong Company and dumped it into the waters of the Rutai Canal and Gumagan River, which is consistent with the quantity of by-product acid from Jinhui Company dumped by Jiangzhong Company as determined by the second-instance judgment in this case. Therefore, the determination of the dumping quantity in the criminal second-instance judgment cannot prove that the main facts or evidence determined by the second-instance judgment in this case are erroneous, does not fall under the circumstances stipulated in Articles 387 and 388 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and is also insufficient to overturn the second-instance judgment.

(5) Whether the second-instance judgment's order that Jinhui Company must deduct 40% of the ecological environment restoration costs upon submission of a certificate of the enterprise's environmental law compliance issued by the environmental protection administrative department, a project completion environmental protection acceptance opinion, and an audit report on technological transformation investment funds issued by a qualified intermediary agency would infringe upon Jinhui Company's independent business operation rights

This case is an environmental civil public interest lawsuit initiated by a social organization for the purpose of protecting the environment and safeguarding the public interest. Its aim is to identify acts of environmental pollution and ecological damage, participate in environmental governance through litigation in an orderly manner, and resolve conflicts and disputes in the field of environmental protection using the rule of law mindset and methods. The courts of first and second instance in this case implemented the basic principles of the Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, prioritized ecological protection and environmental restoration, lawfully determined that the ecological environment was damaged, reasonably determined the ecological environment restoration costs based on the Assessment Technical Report and expert opinions, and lawfully pursued the environmental tort liability of the polluters. At the same time, they fully utilized judicial wisdom and adjudication methods, lawfully and appropriately balanced the conflicts of interest among various parties, and innovated the method of fulfilling the obligation to pay environmental restoration costs. After the second-instance judgment took effect, three of the six defendant enterprises actively fulfilled all contents of the judgment. Although Shimikang Company and Changlong Company once applied to this Court for retrial, they ultimately withdrew their retrial applications. When withdrawing its retrial application, Changlong Company stated that, from the perspective of protecting the environment and safeguarding the public interest, the second-instance judgment was consistent with the enterprise's own development goals. In the process of fulfilling the second-instance judgment, Changlong Company addressed environmental protection issues at their source, investing over RMB 47 million in the construction of environmental projects such as the recycling of by-product acid. These projects have now passed acceptance inspection and are in operation. Currently, Changlong Company has fully fulfilled all contents of the second-instance judgment and recognized that the negative impact the case had on it has been transformed into positive energy for the enterprise to correct its mistakes and fulfill its environmental protection responsibilities. This demonstrates that the second-instance judgment did not interfere with the enterprise's independent business operation rights; on the contrary, it performed the guiding function of evaluation inherent in environmental civil public interest litigation, guiding polluting enterprises to assume their corporate responsibility for environmental protection through technological innovation and transformation.

The purpose of Item 4 of the main text of the second-instance judgment, which orders the six defendant enterprises to deduct 40% of the environmental restoration costs upon submission of a certificate of the enterprise's environmental law compliance issued by the environmental protection administrative department, a project completion environmental protection acceptance opinion, and an audit report on technological transformation investment funds issued by a qualified intermediary agency, is to determine whether Jinhui Company has fully fulfilled its obligation of technological transformation. It is unrelated to the enterprise's independent business operation rights, nor does it set up an approval threshold. Jinhui Company should implement the concept of sustainable development, treat environmental protection as an important factor in its production and operation activities, actively fulfill the contents of the effective judgment, reduce environmental risks through technological transformation, and assume the primary responsibility and social responsibility for environmental protection that an enterprise should bear.

(6) Whether the environmental civil public interest lawsuit filed by the Beijing Chaoyang District Friends of Nature Environmental Institute against other local polluting enterprises would reduce Jinhui Company's liability

Jinhui Company submitted Civil Ruling No. (2015) Tai Zhong Huan Gong Min Su Chu Zi No. 00001 of the Taizhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province and Civil Ruling No. (2015) Su Huan Gong Min Su Zhong Zi No. 00001 of the Jiangsu High People's Court, purportedly to prove that the amount of environmental restoration costs Jinhui Company was ordered to bear in the second-instance judgment was erroneous. Upon examination, the environmental civil public interest lawsuit filed by the Beijing Chaoyang District Friends of Nature Environmental Institute as the plaintiff in the Taizhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province concerning the water pollution of the Gumagan River and Rutai Canal is currently being tried in the first instance. The second-instance judgment in this case calculated the environmental restoration costs Jinhui Company should bear based on the quantity of its by-product acid dumped by Jiangzhong Company, which does not overlap or intersect with the liability of other polluting enterprises. The two civil rulings from other cases submitted by Jinhui Company during the retrial review period do not affect the second-instance judgment's determination of Jinhui Company's environmental tort liability and are not considered new evidence during the retrial review stage. This Court does not accept them.

(7) Whether the second-instance judgment committed an error of law by citing Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law

The second-instance judgment cited the provision of Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law, namely "If the facts found in the original judgment or ruling are clear and the applicable law is correct, the appeal shall be dismissed by judgment or ruling, and the original judgment or ruling shall be affirmed." While affirming the first-instance judgment, it made appropriate adjustments to the time limit and conditions for Jinhui Company to pay the environmental restoration costs. This was not a modification of judgment due to errors in the first-instance judgment, and the application of law was not improper. The adjudication method of the second-instance judgment is conducive to guiding and encouraging enterprises to proactively improve production technology, reduce environmental risks, and decrease environmental pollution at the source. Jinhui Company's assertion that the second-instance judgment erred in law by citing Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law lacks legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

In conclusion, Jinhui Company's application for retrial does not meet the circumstances stipulated in Items 1, 2, 6, and 11 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 204, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows:

The petition for retrial filed by Taixing Jinhui Chemical Co., Ltd. is hereby rejected.
